title: Dr. Bob Sports Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: Dr. Bob Sports review, checked 20 Nov 2026: NFL only prices, no refunds, his own records recomputed by us, and what bettors have said since 2006.
dek: Bob Stoll has sold model based picks as Dr. Bob since 1987. This season he sells only NFL plays, at $825 for the rest of the season or $375 for four weeks, with no refund if they lose. He publishes far more record detail than most sellers, and most of it adds up when we recompute it, but he keeps the books himself and a few totals are one game off.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record of Dr. Bob's plays. The records on this page are the ones his own site publishes. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

short_answer: Dr. Bob Sports is a real, long running business run by one named analyst, Bob Stoll. It lists a mailing address and phone number, publishes its prices and terms, and posts long free analysis of games. Outside coverage backs up the basic story: the Wall Street Journal profiled him in January 2007 and the Daily Racing Form reported in October 2006 that betting lines moved within minutes of his releases. In that sense it is legitimate.

Whether a buyer makes money is a separate question. Dr. Bob publishes more than most sellers: season by season win, loss and push counts going back decades, profit in stars or units, his losing seasons, and a recap of each week's paid plays with the line. We recomputed several of his headline numbers from his own tables on 20 Nov 2026. The college basketball six season total matches exactly, the 2026 NFL split adds up, and the week 10 recap units work out. Two NFL headline totals are each one game off the sum of his own season tables.

So treat the record as careful bookkeeping by the seller, more detailed than most, but not as an audit. No third party holds a time stamped log of every paid play. His 2026 NFL Best Bets stood at 11 and 10 and 1 on 20 Nov 2026, close to break even, while his Strong Opinions carried the season. If you buy, log each play with the line and the time you received it, and compare it with his weekly recap.

guarantee: There is no guarantee. The refund policy says: "Refunds will not be issued based on performance but in some cases refunds are issued based on other circumstances," and points to the terms without saying what those other circumstances are. The terms say a subscriber may cancel at any time "without refund for any prepaid fees," and that a recurring subscription stays active "until the conclusion of the subscription period for which you already have paid."

The terms also say the service is produced "for entertainment purposes only," that "Dr. Bob Sports provides no assurances whatsoever regarding the accuracy of the Service," and that it is provided as is. Neither NFL product page we opened on 20 Nov 2026 says whether the package renews automatically; both are priced as fixed packages.

In plain terms: if the picks lose, you keep the losses and the fee. That is at least clearer than a "guarantee" that only pays in more picks, and the falling season price means a late buyer pays less, but also gets fewer games.

claims_note: How we checked: on 20 Nov 2026 we took the season tables from his past performance page and the 2026 lines from his NFL page, added them by hand, and compared the sums with the headline totals on his homepage, NFL page and product pages. We did not have a game by game list, so we could check that his numbers agree with each other, not that each game was graded correctly.

Most of it holds up. The six season college basketball total matches his table to the play, the 2026 NFL split adds up, and the week 10 units reconcile once you see that plays are sized to win the stated units. That is better bookkeeping than most pick sellers show.

The NFL headlines are each one game off. Best Bets show one more win than his tables support and Strong Opinions show one fewer, so the combined 2016 to 2026 total is right but a game sits in the wrong column. On 7 Nov 2026 we found the same kind of one game gaps, and the recap line on the NFL page still disagrees with the headline by one push. These gaps are small and do not flatter him overall, but they show the record is kept by hand on several pages.

The about page is out of date in places: it says he is embarking on his 33rd year in business and that NFL plays won 59% since 2016 "through 2020", while the homepage says 38 years. It also says that 60% plus winners long term "is no longer possible for anyone", which is a fair warning for anyone reading high win rates elsewhere.

Profit is shown in stars or units, not dollars. The NFL page says Best Bets are 1.0 unit or higher and Strong Opinions are 0.5 unit plays. The past performance page also lists bad stretches: NFL Best Bets at 50.6% from 1999 through 2012, after which he says he "decided to stop handicapping the NFL until I had a better model" and returned in 2016, a 2023 college football Best Bets season of 35-33-2 for minus 9.7 stars, and four losing seasons for his former NBA Guru. The Daily Racing Form reported in 2006 that his 2005 NFL plays went 26 and 35, which fits that weak stretch. Publishing losing years is a point in his favor, but the seller still chooses how the record is presented.
record: What is independently verifiable: we found no third party that holds a time stamped log of Dr. Bob's paid plays, no contest results run by an organizer, and no regulator or court record about the business. What outside reporting does confirm is his influence on lines in the mid 2000s. The Daily Racing Form reported on 19 Oct 2006 that he emailed college picks to clients at 10 a.m. Pacific on Thursdays, that Pinnacle took his games off the board within minutes, and that eight games moved at least a point within half an hour. A Wall Street Journal profile of 5 Jan 2007, reposted on TheRX, said packages then ran from $25 to $2,495 and that 10 casinos moved one bowl line by up to two points within 78 seconds.

What the seller publishes, and how a buyer could check it: the past performance page has season by season tables (wins, losses, pushes and stars, split by star rating for college football and basketball), and the NFL page posts a recap of the week's paid plays with the side or total, the line and the result. On 20 Nov 2026 the week 10 recap listed five plays: Washington +2.5, Kansas City and Atlanta over 45.5, Houston and Cleveland under 41.5 at -115 (a loss), Minnesota and Green Bay under 41.5, and Carolina +2.5. This is more detail than most pick sellers show. But we saw only the current week's recap and season totals, not a complete dated archive of every play with its release time and line, and the release page is locked to subscribers.

Line movement cuts both ways for a buyer. The 2006 article said plays bet after the line moved still went 40 and 24 and 7 that season, but a buyer who gets a worse number than the posted line will not match the posted record. Several reviewers on HandicappingReviews.org between 2015 and 2021 complained about exactly that.
Either way, the record is kept by the seller. Until a third party holds the log, every percentage on the site is his own bookkeeping, careful as it is.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition Dr. Bob Sports is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how its plays perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Dr. Bob's NFL page claims 57.5% on Best Bets since 2016, and his 2026 Best Bets stood at 11 and 10 and 1 on 20 Nov 2026. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Dr. Bob Sports is thin and mostly old. Over about 20 years we found one review site with buyer comments, two Sportsbook Review threads, two Las Vegas Advisor discussions and two TheRX threads. We found no Reddit discussion of the service in our archive searches, and no Trustpilot or BBB profile we could confirm. Below is all of it and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found about a dozen independent posts about Dr. Bob across HandicappingReviews.org, Sportsbook Review, the Las Vegas Advisor and TheRX, spread from 2007 to 2026, plus older press coverage. The pattern is consistent: people respect his method and his openness, and even critics rarely call him dishonest, but buyers who say they paid describe average or losing results, lines that moved before they could bet, and a high price for the bankroll needed. A 2014 Sportsbook Review buyer called his subscription terrible; others in the same thread said his results were average but not a fraud. Positive buyer comments praise customer service and his willingness to explain his methods. No poster published a full record of a paid package, and almost nothing is recent: the only 2026 post we found was a forum member asking whether anyone had his best bets.

In a TheRX thread where members discuss plays from paid services, one member asked whether anyone had Dr. Bob's best bets. Nobody answered in the thread. It shows his plays still circulate among bettors, nothing more.

When the Wall Street Journal profile was reposted on TheRX, one member called him "the main man right now" while another said his hot streak had cooled to about 51%, though still respectable. A third asked where that 51% came from. Nobody in the thread said they subscribed.

On HandicappingReviews.org, a reviewer who said they bought full season NFL and basketball packages and lost a significant sum wrote that they asked for a discount to continue and was turned down. They called Dr. Bob honest and hard working but questioned his concern for clients. Posters on this site are not verified.

Other reviews on the same page, the latest dated 1 Jan 2021, complain that lines moved before they could bet the plays, that the service is expensive for the bankroll needed, and of poor customer service. One reviewer said they lost a lot of money in four weeks.

The same page also has positive reviews: praise for customer service and for sharing methods with subscribers, and a longtime follower who said they wished they had won more but could not complain. None of these reviews give records or amounts.

A Sportsbook Review thread with an accusing title was started by a buyer who called the picks "terrible" and objected that Stoll is not a doctor. Other members replied that the nickname comes from basketball and that his results are average but he is not a fraud; one said they lost their bankroll on an earlier subscription. No logs were posted.

In a Las Vegas Advisor answer, the bettor Fezzik credited Dr. Bob with building a following by winning "without hype", then argued his results had fallen for about five years as the market caught up with his methods. This is an old opinion based on his published numbers.

In a Las Vegas Advisor forum thread on the same theme, several members respected his work but disliked how he presented his record, and one claimed he had once stopped counting the juice in a losing year. Others in the thread disagreed on whether that was dishonest. No evidence was posted and we did not verify it.

We found no Reddit thread about the service in our archive searches, no Trustpilot page and no Better Business Bureau profile we could confirm belongs to drbobsports.com, and no buyer account from 2025 or 2026 describing results.

conflicts: We saw no sportsbook affiliate links, promo codes or revenue share offers on the Dr. Bob Sports pages we opened on 20 Nov 2026.

The NBA page sends readers to KillerCappers.com, where his former NBA handicapper now sells picks, and quotes that handicapper's recent record. We saw no statement about whether Dr. Bob Sports is paid for that referral. The NFL 4 Weeks product page also lists EVBettor as an analyst alongside Dr. Bob, without saying who EVBettor is or how the two share the plays.
He gives a free weekly NFL bet as a guest on the VSiN show A Numbers Game. That is promotion for his paid service as well as free content.
strengths: A named analyst, an LLC operator, a mailing address and a phone number, with prices and refund terms in writing.
Publishes far more than most sellers: decades of season by season records including losing years, and a weekly recap of the paid plays with the line and result.
His numbers mostly reconcile. The six season college basketball total, the 2026 NFL split and the week 10 units all add up exactly when we recompute them from his own pages.
Outside press from 2006 and 2007 (Daily Racing Form, Wall Street Journal) confirms the market moved on his plays, which is rare evidence that bettors took him seriously.
Long free game analysis is posted for games outside the paid package, so a reader can judge the method before paying.
The season price drops week by week, so a late buyer is not charged for games already played.
concerns: The record is kept by the seller, and two NFL headline totals are each one game off the sum of his own tables.
No refund if the picks lose, and cancelling does not refund prepaid fees.
His 2026 NFL Best Bets, the plays he rates highest, stood at 11 and 10 and 1 on 20 Nov 2026, about break even before the fee.
Bettors have long reported that his lines move fast after release, so a buyer may not get the posted number and will not match the posted record.
Old basketball package prices are still posted although the site says he is not handicapping basketball this season, and the about page is years out of date.
Almost all independent buyer comment is more than five years old, so there is little recent evidence either way.
checklist: Read his free game analysis for a few weeks before paying, and compare it with the plays he posts in his weekly recap.
Write down each play the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get and the time. Compare your number with the line in his recap.
Check his posted season totals against his past performance tables yourself; it takes ten minutes and shows whether the books still agree.
Size bets the way he does: his units are amounts to win, so a 1 unit play at -115 risks 1.15 units.
Buy late in the season only if the lower price still makes sense for the number of games left.
Remember there is no refund for losses and no refund of prepaid fees if you cancel.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real business run by Bob Stoll since 1987, with a named operator, an address, published prices and written terms, and the Wall Street Journal and Daily Racing Form covered him in 2006 and 2007. That makes it legitimate as a business; it does not prove the picks make money for buyers today.
How much does Dr. Bob Sports cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 the NFL season package was $825, a price the site lowers each week as the season runs down (it was $995 on 27 Oct and $895 on 7 Nov), and the NFL 4 Weeks package was $375. Those were the only packages offered this season, and losses are not refunded.
Does Dr. Bob Sports have a verified record?

No third party verifies it. He publishes detailed season tables and a weekly recap of the paid plays with lines. When we recomputed his totals, most matched his own tables exactly and two NFL totals were each one game off, but the record is still kept by the seller.
What is Dr. Bob's NFL record this season?

His NFL page showed 31 and 21 and 2 for plus 3.77 units on 20 Nov 2026: Best Bets 11 and 10 and 1 and Strong Opinions 20 and 11 and 1. Those are his own figures; we checked that they add up, not each game.

Not for losing picks. The refund policy says refunds are not issued based on performance, and the terms say you can cancel at any time without a refund of prepaid fees. Some refunds for other circumstances are mentioned but not explained.
Is Dr. Bob Sports worth it?

For the money you get every NFL Best Bet and Strong Opinion with written analysis, sent at release, from an analyst who publishes losing years and whose numbers mostly reconcile. What is unproven is whether those plays still beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 at the lines a buyer can actually get, after a fee of several hundred dollars, and there is no refund if they do not.
